newsitem.title: USA: Texas bank regulator touted for FDIC job - sources.
newsitem.headline: Texas bank regulator touted for FDIC job - sources.

text.p: The Clinton administration is considering nominating Texas Banking Commissioner Catherine Ghiglieri for the top job at the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp, sources familiar with the agency said.
Rep Henry Gonzalez, Democrat of Texas, gave his support to Ghiglieri for the FDIC chairmanship in a June 11 letter to President Bill Clinton.

"Ms Ghiglieri has the ideal background for the position and has my unconditional endorsement," the ranking Democrat on the House Banking Committee wrote, according to a copy of the letter obtained by Reuters.
"She has impressed myself, and I am sure my committee colleagues, in the course of her appearances before the committee and her work on various banking issues," Gonzalez added.
A White House spokesman declined to comment on any possible nominations and said no announcement on the FDIC chairmanship was "imminent."
Appointed banking commissioner in 1992, Ghiglieri is responsible for overseeing 450 state-chartered banks with assets of $51 billion.
Before working at the state level, Ghiglieri spent almost two decades with the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.
Ghiglieri's possible nomination was reported in the newspaper American Banker on Monday.
If nominated and approved for the top FDIC job, Ghiglieri would replace acting Chairman Andrew Hove, who took over when Ricki Helfer left the agency on June 1.
